subject: Post-demo: BrightCart burst capacity & overage terms
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@brightcart.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T14:32:00-08:00
Subject: Post-demo recap — BrightCart burst capacity & next steps

Hi Amira / Tomas —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can produce a clean pricing path and quota proposal: 

Summary of what I heard on the call
- Primary use: checkout personalization + post-purchase messaging (inference per user event)
- Expected steady-state volume: 40–80M generated tokens / month (range depends on ramp & personalization depth)
- Peak/burst behavior: short spikes tied to promotions — up to ~3–4x baseline for 15–30 minute windows (rough estimate)
- Target unit economics: you mentioned aiming for ~$8–$12 per 1M tokens as a target for the pilot budget

Clarifying asks (so our quote maps to your budget):
1) Can you confirm a single typical request token count (prompt + expected gen)? If you have a sample payload we can use it to run an accurate token estimate.
2) What percentage of calls need sub-200ms p50 latency vs. <500ms? (helps decide routing to low-latency vs cost-tier models)
3) Do you want burst to be throttled (soft degrade) or buffered (allow short overage then bill) if you exceed reserved quota?

What I’ll do next:
- Share a short template for 30/60/90-day token history (attached) — if you can fill the last 30 days we’ll firm up the unit estimate.
- Draft two pricing scenarios: (A) conservative reserved capacity with a 20% day-of spike buffer, and (B) pay-as-you-go with explicit overage tiers for bursts.
- Include examples for total $/1M tokens and projected spend at low/median/high throughput.

Attachments: BrightCart_usage_template.csv (please fill in any recent numbers)

If this looks right, can we target Thursday 12/17 at 10am PT for a short follow-up to review the draft pricing?

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0187

Sean — thanks for the clear notes. A few quick answers below and a couple of extra asks: 

Answers:
- Typical request size: prompt ~90 tokens, generation ~140 tokens (so ~230 tokens per inference on average) — I attached a sample payload in a follow-up.
- Latency needs: for checkout personalization we need p50 <250ms and p95 <600ms for top 10% of traffic; background jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Burst preference: we’d prefer buffered bursts (allow short overage) rather than hard throttling — loss of personalization during a sale hurts conversion.

Extra asks:
- Can you include an explicit example of a 10-minute 3x burst showing cost and whether we would be throttled?
- What’s the process and lead time for a quota increase if we scale faster than expected?
- Any pilot discounts or introductory spike credits available?

We can do 12/17 at 10am PT. Please include someone from your finance/ops who can walk through the overage math.

—Amira
Amira Hassan
Head of Growth | BrightCart
amira@brightcart.com | +1 (646) 555-2121

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Amira Hassan <amira@brightcart.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Tomas Rivera <tomas@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — BrightCart burst capacity & next steps

Amira — great, thanks for the details. Short answers up front, then a concrete example and next steps.

1) Burst handling model we recommend
- Default: soft quota with automatic buffering. Short bursts (up to a configurable % of reserved capacity) are allowed and billed as overage. For sustained exceedances we fall back to a cost-tier model or graceful degradation per rule set.
- For pilots we can enable a 20% spike buffer for first 90 days at no additional setup cost; any tokens above buffer are billed at the overage rate in the quote.

2) Quota increase process and lead time
- Self-service increases in Console for up to +50% immediate; larger increases are request-based and typically 3–5 business days to provision dedicated capacity (or faster with burst credits). We’ll include steps in the quote.

3) Pilot credits / intro promos
- We can offer a $10k spike credit for pilots under the BrightCart proof-of-concept (applies to overage only, not base reserved commit). I’ll confirm with RevOps in the quote.

Concrete 10-minute 3x burst example (based on your ~230 tokens per call):
- Baseline steady throughput: 200 requests/min -> ~46k tokens/min -> ~2.76M tokens/hour
- 3x burst for 10 minutes: additional ~92k tokens/min for 10 min -> ~920k extra tokens total
- If your reserved capacity includes a 20% spike buffer, that buffer would absorb X of the extra tokens; remaining tokens billed as overage.
- Example pricing (illustrative): base unit price $10 / 1M tokens, overage price 2x base ($20 / 1M tokens). 920k tokens * $20/1M = $18.40 for that 10-minute burst above buffer. If we applied pilot credit, that $18.40 would be deducted from the $10k spike credit.

Notes: the numbers above are illustrative — I’ll produce a short spreadsheet with low/med/high scenarios (attached) and two concrete quote lines: reserved + spike buffer, and pay-as-you-go with explicit overage tiers.

Attachments: RDW-pricing-examples.pdf (sample scenarios)

Next steps: I’ll circulate the draft quote by EOD Wednesday 12/16 so we have time to review before our call on 12/17. If you want us to tighten the latency SLAs for checkout traffic, call that out and we’ll add a low-latency routing premium in the quote.

Looping Dev for ops provisioning notes.

Thanks —
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
